In type 1 diabetes, the immune system attacks and destroys the beta cells in the pancreas, which leads to a lack of insulin production. In type 2 diabetes, the body becomes resistant to insulin, and the pancreas produces insufficient amounts of insulin to maintain normal blood sugar levels. This can be caused by a combination of factors, such as obesity, sedentary lifestyle, and genetic predisposition. In type 2 diabetes, oral medications, lifestyle changes, and sometimes insulin therapy are used to manage the condition.

In both types of diabetes, the underlying factors that contribute to the development of the disease can be complex and multifactorial. Understanding the pathogenesis of diabetes is crucial for developing effective prevention and treatment strategies.
